checks.message: The return memo is more than 30 days old. Section 138(b) requires the notice within 30 days of receiving the information from the bank; consult a lawyer before relying on this notice.

document.heading: LEGAL NOTICE UNDER SECTION 138 OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881
document.mode_of_delivery: By Registered Post A.D. / Speed Post / Email
document.subject: Notice of dishonour of cheque no. {cheque_no} dated {cheque_date} for Rs. {cheque_amount}
intro: I, {sender_name}, residing at {sender_address}, hereby serve upon you the following notice:
pre_facts: You issued cheque no. {cheque_no} dated {cheque_date} for Rs. {cheque_amount} ({cheque_amount_words}), drawn on {bank_name}, in my favour, towards discharge of your legally enforceable debt or liability, namely: {debt_reason}.

I presented the said cheque for payment on {presentation_date}[[ through my bank, {payee_bank}]], within its period of validity. The cheque was returned unpaid with the remark "{return_reason}" by return memo dated {return_memo_date}.

The dishonour of the cheque for the above reason constitutes an offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. This notice is issued within 30 days of receipt of the information from the bank regarding the dishonour, as required by Section 138(b) of the Act.
paragraphs: I therefore call upon you to pay the said sum of Rs. {cheque_amount} to me within 15 (fifteen) days of receipt of this notice.

Take notice that if you fail to make the payment within the said period, I shall be constrained to file a criminal complaint against you under Section 138 read with Section 142 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, which is punishable with imprisonment of up to two years, or fine of up to twice the amount of the cheque, or both, and to initiate civil proceedings for recovery of the amount with interest and costs, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences.
A copy of this notice has been retained for record and further action.

court_heading: BEFORE THE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION
document.heading: COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019
intro: The Complainant respectfully submits as under:
pre_facts: The Complainant is a consumer within the meaning of Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, having purchased/availed {product_service} from the Opposite Party on {purchase_date} for a consideration of Rs. {amount_paid}[[ vide invoice/order no. {invoice_no}]], for personal use and not for any commercial purpose.

paragraphs.text: The Complainant raised the grievance with the Opposite Party on {complaint_date}, but the Opposite Party failed to redress it.
The Complainant also sent a legal notice to the Opposite Party on {notice_date}, but the Opposite Party failed to comply with it.

paragraphs: The above acts and omissions of the Opposite Party amount to defect in goods, deficiency in service and/or unfair trade practice within the meaning of Sections 2(10), 2(11) and 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which has caused the Complainant financial loss, harassment and mental agony.

paragraphs.text: The relevant provisions of law also include: {legal_provisions}.

paragraphs: This Commission has territorial jurisdiction under Section 34(2) of the Act, as the Complainant resides or personally works for gain within its jurisdiction and/or the cause of action arose here. The value of the goods or services paid as consideration is within the pecuniary jurisdiction of this Commission.

The cause of action arose on {purchase_date} and subsequently when the Opposite Party failed to redress the grievance. The complaint is filed within the period of two years prescribed under Section 69 of the Act.
document.prayer_intro: It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Commission may be pleased to direct the Opposite Party to:
prayer: refund / pay Rs. {refund_amount} to the Complainant, along with interest from the date of payment till realisation, or replace the goods / remove the defect;
pay Rs. {compensation_amount} as compensation for the harassment and mental agony suffered by the Complainant;
[[pay Rs. {litigation_cost} towards the costs of litigation;]]
discontinue the unfair trade practice; and
grant any other relief that this Hon'ble Commission deems fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
verification: I, {complainant_name}, the Complainant above named, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {para_count} of the above complaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge and belief, and nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

document.heading: APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 12 OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ACT, 2005
intro: The Applicant respectfully submits as under:
pre_facts: The Applicant is {relationship}[[, having been married on {marriage_date}]]. The Applicant and the Respondents lived together in a shared household at {shared_household}. The Applicant is therefore an 'aggrieved person' in a 'domestic relationship' with the Respondents within the meaning of Section 2 of the Act.

pre_facts.text: The following children were born from the relationship: {children}.

pre_facts: The Respondents have subjected the Applicant to domestic violence as defined in Section 3 of the Act, as detailed below.

paragraphs.text: A Domestic Incident Report was recorded on {dir_date}, a copy of which is enclosed.

paragraphs: Under Section 17 of the Act, the Applicant has the right to reside in the shared household irrespective of any right, title or interest in it, and cannot be evicted except in accordance with the procedure established by law, as affirmed by the Supreme Court in Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja, (2021) 1 SCC 414.

The Applicant apprehends further violence and is in urgent need of protection and relief. This Hon'ble Court has jurisdiction as the Applicant resides / the Respondents reside / the cause of action arose within its local limits, in terms of Section 27 of the Act.
document.prayer_intro: It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to:

prayer.text: pass a protection order under Section 18 prohibiting the Respondents from committing any act of domestic violence, from contacting or communicating with the Applicant, entering her place of work, and from alienating assets or operating joint bank accounts;

pass a residence order under Section 19 restraining the Respondents from dispossessing the Applicant from the shared household or, in the alternative, directing them to provide alternate accommodation of the same standard;

direct the Respondents under Section 20 to pay monetary relief for the expenses and losses suffered by the Applicant, and maintenance[[ of Rs. {monetary_amount} per month]] for the Applicant and her children;
grant temporary custody of the minor children to the Applicant under Section 21;
direct the Respondents to pay compensation and damages for injuries, including mental torture and emotional distress, under Section 22;
direct the Respondents to return the Applicant's stridhan, jewellery and articles, namely: {stridhan};
pass interim and ex parte orders under Section 23 pending disposal of this application; and

prayer: pass any other order that this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the interest of justice.
verification: I, {aggrieved_name}, the Applicant above named, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {para_count} of the above application are true and correct to my knowledge and belief, and nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

document.subject: Complaint regarding {incident_type} and request for registration of FIR under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
intro: I, {complainant_name}, residing at {complainant_address}, respectfully submit this complaint for registration of a First Information Report in respect of the following incident, which took place on {incident_date}[[ at about {incident_time}]] at {incident_place}.

paragraphs.text: The details of the accused person(s), as known to me, are: {accused_details}.
As a result of the incident I have suffered the following loss/injury: {loss_details}.

legal_basis: The above facts disclose the commission of cognizable offence(s). Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence must be reduced to writing and registered, and as held by the Supreme Court in Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh, (2014) 2 SCC 1, registration of an FIR is mandatory in such cases.

legal_basis.text: The relevant provisions of law include: {legal_provisions}.

document.prayer_intro: I therefore request you to kindly:
prayer: register a First Information Report under the appropriate provisions of law and investigate the matter;
provide me a free copy of the FIR as required under Section 173(2) of the BNSS, 2023;
take appropriate legal action against the accused person(s) and ensure the safety of myself and my family; and
keep me informed of the progress of the investigation as required under Section 193(3) of the BNSS, 2023.
closing: I declare that the information given above is true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief.

document.subject: Complaint under Section 173(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 against refusal by Police Station {police_station} to register an FIR regarding {incident_type}
intro: I, {complainant_name}, residing at {complainant_address}, respectfully submit as follows:
paragraphs: The above incident took place on {incident_date} at {incident_place}, within the jurisdiction of Police Station {police_station}.

On {date_approached}, I approached Police Station {police_station}[[ and met {officer_name}]] with a written complaint and requested registration of an FIR. However, the officer in charge did not register the FIR. {refusal_details}
legal_basis: The information disclosed by me relates to cognizable offence(s). Registration of an FIR in such cases is mandatory under Section 173 of the BNSS, 2023, as held by the Supreme Court in Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh, (2014) 2 SCC 1.

Under Section 173(4) of the BNSS, 2023, a person aggrieved by such refusal may send the substance of the information in writing and by post to the Superintendent of Police, who shall, if satisfied that it discloses a cognizable offence, investigate the case or direct an investigation.

legal_basis.text: The relevant provisions of law include: {legal_provisions}.

document.prayer_intro: I therefore request you to kindly:
prayer: direct the registration of an FIR on my complaint and a fair investigation, or investigate the case yourself;
take appropriate action against the officer(s) responsible for refusing to register the FIR; and
provide me a copy of the FIR and keep me informed of the progress of the investigation.
closing: I declare that the information given above is true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief.

document.subject: Claim for unpaid wages of Rs. {amount_due} against {employer_name}
intro: I, {employee_name}, residing at {employee_address}, respectfully submit this claim against my employer, {employer_name}, {employer_address}, as follows:
pre_facts: I was employed with {employer_name} as {designation} from {joining_date}[[ to {leaving_date}]] at a monthly salary of Rs. {monthly_salary}.
The employer has failed to pay my wages for the period {unpaid_period}, amounting to a total of Rs. {amount_due} ({amount_due_words}).
legal_basis: Under Section 17 of the Code on Wages, 2019, monthly wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month, and where an employee has been removed, dismissed, retrenched or has resigned, the wages payable must be paid within two working days.
Under Section 18 of the Code, no deductions other than those authorised may be made from wages. Under Section 45, an employee may file a claim before the authority for unpaid or delayed wages.

legal_basis.text: The relevant provisions of law also include: {legal_provisions}.

document.prayer_intro: I therefore request you to kindly:
prayer: direct the employer to pay the unpaid wages of Rs. {amount_due};
award compensation for the delayed payment as permissible under the Code;

prayer.text: direct the employer to settle all final dues, including leave encashment, gratuity (if applicable) and the experience / relieving letter; and

prayer: pass any other order that you deem fit in the interest of justice.
closing: I declare that the information given above is true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief.
